'''Andrew Victor Sutherland''' is an American [[mathematician]] and Senior Research Scientist at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]].{{r|mit}}  His research focuses on computational aspects of [[number theory]] and [[arithmetic geometry]].{{r|mit}} He is known for his contributions to several projects involving large scale computations, including the [[Polymath project]] on bounded gaps between primes,{{r|quantagaps}}{{r|dsgaps}}{{r|amsgaps}}{{r|polymath1}}{{r|polymath2}} the L-functions and Modular Forms Database,{{r|mitlmfdb}}{{r|dslmfdb}} the [[sums of three cubes]] project,{{r|mit42}}{{r|newsci42}}{{r|pop2019}} and the computation and classification of [[Sato-Tate conjecture|Sato-Tate distributions]].{{r|gcp}}{{r|aws}}{{r|g2class}}{{r|stg2}}

==Education and career==
Sutherland earned a bachelor's degree in mathematics from MIT in 1990.{{r|mit}}  Following an entrepreneurial career in the software industry he returned to MIT and completed his doctoral degree in mathematics in 2007 under the supervision of [[Michael Sipser]] and [[Ronald Rivest]], winning the George M. Sprowls prize for his thesis.{{r|mit}}{{r|mathgen}}  He joined the MIT mathematics department as a research scientist in 2009. He was promoted to principal research scientist in 2012, and then to senior research scientist in 2024.{{r|mit}}

He is one of the principal investigators in the Simons Collaboration on Arithmetic Geometry, Number Theory, and Computation, a large multi-university collaboration involving [[Boston University]], [[Brown University|Brown]], [[Harvard]], MIT, and [[Dartmouth College]],{{r|simons}} and he currently serves as an associate editor of ''[[Mathematics of Computation]]'', editor in chief of ''[[Research in Number Theory]]'',{{r|rnt}} managing editor of the L-functions and Modular Forms Database,{{r|lmfdb}} and president of the [[Number Theory Foundation]].{{r|ntf}}

==Contributions==

Sutherland has developed or improved several methods for [[counting points on elliptic curves]] and [[hyperelliptic curve]]s, that have applications to [[elliptic curve cryptography]], [[hyperelliptic curve cryptography]], [[elliptic curve primality proving]], and the computation of [[L-functions]].{{r|lseries}}{{r|dlog}}{{r|hcp}}{{r|cm}}  These include improvements to the [[Schoof–Elkies–Atkin algorithm]]{{r|modpoly}}{{r|emodpoly}} that led to new point-counting records{{r|pcrecord}}, and average polynomial-time algorithms for computing [[zeta functions]] of hyperelliptic curves over [[finite fields]], developed jointly with David Harvey.{{r|avpoly1}}{{r|avpoly2}}{{r|avpoly3}}

Much of Sutherland's research involves the application of fast point-counting algorithms to numerically investigate generalizations of the [[Sato-Tate conjecture]] regarding the distribution of point counts for a curve (or [[abelian variety]]) defined over the rational numbers (or a [[number field]]) when reduced modulo prime numbers of increasing size.{{r|lseries}}{{r|random}}{{r|twist}}{{r|fk}}.  It is conjectured that these distributions can be described by [[random matrix]] models using a "Sato-Tate group" associated to the curve by a construction of [[J.-P. Serre|Serre]].{{r|ks}}{{r|nxp}}  In 2012 Francesc Fite, [[Kiran Kedlaya]], Victor Rotger and Sutherland classified the Sato-Tate groups that arise for genus 2 curves and abelian varieties of dimension 2,{{r|g2class}} and in 2019 Fite, Kedlaya, and Sutherland announced a similar classification to abelian varieties of dimension 3.{{r|g3class}}

In the process of studying these classifications, Sutherland compiled several large data sets of curves and then worked with [[Andrew Booker (mathematician)|Andrew Booker]] and others to compute their [[L-functions]] and incorporate them into the L-functions and Modular Forms Database.{{r|gcp}}{{r|g2db}}{{r|g3db}}  More recently, Booker and Sutherland resolved Mordell's question regarding the representation of 3 as a sum of three cubes.{{r|quanta3}}{{r|ams3}}{{r|newsci3}}

==Recognition==
Sutherland was named to the 2021 class of fellows of the American Mathematical Society "for contributions to number theory, both on the theoretical and computational aspects of the subject".<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.ams.org/cgi-bin/fellows/fellows_by_year.cgi?year=2021|title=2021 Class of Fellows of the AMS|publisher=American Mathematical Society|access-date=2020-11-02}}</ref>  He was selected to deliver the [[Cahit Arf#Arf Lectures|Arf Lecture]] in 2022.<ref>{{citation|url=https://math.metu.edu.tr/en/arf-lectures|title=Arf Lectures|publisher=Middle East Technical University|access-date=2020-11-17}}</ref> and the [[N.G.W.H. Beeger#Beeger Lectures|Beeger Lecture]] in 2024.<ref>{{citation|url=https://mathematischcongres.nl/nmc-2024/beeger-lecture-2024/|title=Beeger Lecture|publisher=Nederlands Mathematische Congres|access-date=2024-04-03}}</ref>
